text:
sarah: Hey network folks — quick follow-up. Customer wants outbound requests from our Private deployment to always come from a stable IP so they can allowlist webhooks. Options I can think of: per-tenant EIP, shared NAT with mapping, or a proxy inside their VPC. Thoughts? cc @anna @mike

anna: Per-tenant EIP is the simplest for customers (obviously isolated) but costs / EIP quotas blow up for hundreds of tenants. Also adds burden for IP reclamation on churn.

mike: Another pattern: keep a small pool of EIPs per-region and assign 1:1 for high-tier tenants, let mid/low tiers share IPs. Requires a mapping service in the control plane and fast propagation to route/NAT layer.

julian: Security note — shared egress means we need strict tenant-level logging, and a way to instantly revoke if a tenant is deprovisioned. Also ensure no cross-tenant source-port collisions if we do port-based overlays.

rachel: From sales: regulated customers (fin/health) will want dedicated public IPs. This can be an upsell. But non-regulated customers will prefer cheaper shared options.

infra-bot: natted-alloc-service created PR #542: adds allocation API + simple release endpoint. CI green.

mike: Cost numbers for AWS: NAT Gateway ~ $0.045/hr + data processed fees, per-EIP nat via TGW+ECMP has other tradeoffs. If we run EC2-based NAT instances we can drop cost on steady high throughput but increase ops/ops-sla surface.

anna: Another design: provide a per-customer sidecar relay that runs inside the customer's VPC. Traffic would originate from their subnet so they inherently get a stable egress IP. Pro: no EIP management for us; Con: heavier onboarding and more things we don't control.

sarah: Quick tradeoff recap:
- Dedicated EIP per-customer: simple, predictable for customer, expensive and hits quotas.
- Regional pool + 1:1 assignment: cheaper, requires mapping/stateful service and careful churn handling.
- In-VPC sidecar/proxy: preserves IP, shifts infra responsibility to customer, complicates support.
- Peering/PrivateLink with SNAT on customer side: similar to sidecar but less install (they handle SNAT).

mike: Example iptables SNAT config we'd run on a sidecar if we go that route:

```
# on sidecar host in customer VPC
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 3.101.45.210
```

julian: Also callout: we need per-tenant flow logs (VPC/ENI flow logs or our proxy logs) and an audit trail for allocation/release events. Retention and access controls must be defined in the RFC.

sarah: Proposed decision for now: implement regional EIP pools + tiered 1:1 mapping as the default cost/perf option, plus an opt-in paid "dedicated EIP" add-on for enterprise customers. For strictly regulated customers, recommend PrivateLink/peering + customer-side SNAT or a managed sidecar.

mike: I'll own a spike to model EIP counts, cost (NAT gateway vs EC2 NAT vs proxy), and churn behavior. Will produce a short doc with numbers and a proof-of-concept allocator by EOW.

anna: I'll draft an RFC for the allocation service (API, reconciliation loop, failure modes) and list required logging hooks + integration points with the control plane.

sarah: :thumbsup: thanks. Let's sync this into Thurs architecture slot and capture any objections.

rachel: FYI I'll surface the dedicated-EIP addon idea to a few AE conversations and collect willingness-to-pay intel.

infra-bot: created task INF-882: "egress-ip allocation spike" assigned to @mike.

mike: starting spike now, will post interim notes in the doc.
